description: Which Georgia public school attendance zones (elementary, middle, high) contain a place, or (attendance_rules=true) how attendance zones work in Georgia. Give exactly one of: lat and lon; an address (located with the U.S. Census Geocoder, an outside service); a 2020 census tract_geoid (every zone covering the tract with the share of its 2020 population in each, or, when none does, a coverage_reason); or attendance_rules=true with no place. Optional grade (pk, k, 01-12) and year. Returns the district, the zoned schools with names and where each zone came from (method, accuracy_class, positional_rmse_m, boundary_vintage, currency_status, currency_note, source_url), a level_status per school level, a coverage_status (zoned; gap: some level has no zone there; one_school_per_grade; not_available: the district publishes no zones at some level, with the reason; not_zoned: no zone assigns the grade asked, i.e. pre-K), a currency_warning when a zone's source predates an adopted change that could not be applied, an overlap_warning when two schools' zones cover the point for the same grades, the point's tract and county, and a geojson_url per zone (never the shapes themselves). Zones are rebuilt from published sources of varying currency and are not an official enrollment determination; families confirm with the district. The zoned school is the default assignment (assignment_note). attendance_rules=true returns instead who draws zones and the main ways a student attends a public school other than the zoned one, with the statute or rule behind each, for questions about how zones work. A dated summary, not legal advice; lang="es" gives it in Spanish. Addresses and points are never stored or logged.
